title_en: What time was the meetup again
jp_sentences: あれ、明日の約束は何時からだっけ。
集まる場所の名前も忘れてしまった。
確か駅の近くの店だったよね。
先週も同じことを聞いたっけ。
悪いけど、もう一度教えて。
jp: あれ、明日の約束は何時からだっけ。集まる場所の名前も忘れてしまった。確か駅の近くの店だったよね。先週も同じことを聞いたっけ。悪いけど、もう一度教えて。着いたら電話するね。
translation_pt: Ué, o combinado de amanhã era a partir de que horas mesmo? Também esqueci o nome do lugar onde a gente vai se encontrar. Era aquele lugar perto da estação, né? Será que eu já perguntei a mesma coisa semana passada? Foi mal, me fala de novo. Quando eu chegar eu te ligo.
translation_en: Huh, what time was tomorrow's plan supposed to start again? I've forgotten the name of the place we're meeting at too. It was that place near the station, right? Did I ask you the same thing last week too? Sorry, tell me one more time. I'll call you when I get there.

grammar_target_label.pt-BR: 〜っけ (era... mesmo?, tentando puxar da memória)
grammar_target_label.en: ~kke (what was it again?, trying to recall)

authoring_note: One text: a casual message a learner would send a friend the night before meeting up. Single speaker, plain casual register throughout (the register っけ requires), opening with あれ like the lesson's own model and closing on 着いたら電話するね. っけ appears twice in its two licensed formations: noun + だっけ (何時からだっけ) and casual past verb + っけ (聞いたっけ). No bank sentence fit inside this single text; the eight っけ sentences in the bank are unrelated one-liners and stitching them would break the one-situation rule, so the passage is authored.
